title: Pipeline: IF/ELSE parse+render
notes: Extend the canonical pipeline script v2 grammar to support Scratch-like conditional containers: `IF <expr>` and optional `ELSE`. Persist as nested `pipeline_ast` nodes (e.g., `{kind:'if', expr, then_children, else_children}`) and ensure render -> parse roundtrips. Keep runner semantics as a stub (treat IF as executing `then_children` only) but ensure script<->AST translation is correct and errors/warnings are clear.
acceptance: Backend parser accepts `IF <expr>` with indented children and optional `ELSE` at same indent, and returns `pipeline_ast` with an if-node.
Renderer emits canonical formatting for IF/ELSE with 2-space indentation per level.
Roundtrip unit test added: script -> ast -> script preserves structure for IF/ELSE nesting under ROUND/FOREACH_TASK/FOREACH_ACTION.
Validation endpoint `/api/pipeline/validate` reports helpful errors for malformed IF/ELSE (missing expr, ELSE without IF, empty blocks).
No TCP binds required; `python3 -m py_compile` and the new unit test pass.

title: PWA: insert FOREACH_ACTION + IF/ELSE blocks
notes: Add first-class UI actions to insert `FOREACH_ACTION` and `IF/ELSE` containers from the blocks toolbar (wrap selected or append). Ensure delete behavior remains correct (deleting a container splices children up; editor prevents empty containers by auto-inserting a STEP placeholder). Keep scope limited to block editing + script sync; no runner behavior changes.
acceptance: Blocks toolbar has buttons to insert `FOREACH_ACTION` and `IF` (with optional default ELSE).
Insertion works for wrap-selected and append-root cases, updating the canonical script textarea immediately.
Deleting IF/ELSE and FOREACH_ACTION containers behaves predictably (children spliced up; no invalid empty containers).
Keyboard delete still works for selected blocks.
Any new UI strings are added to i18n for: en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ko, vi, ar, fr, es, ru, de.
`node --check autonovelwriter/pwa/app.js` passes.

title: Action Library: update API (copy-on-edit)
notes: Add a minimal backend endpoint to update action templates. If the target action is a default, updates must create a new user action (copy-on-edit) and return the new id. If the target action is user-origin, update in-place. Keep validation shallow but ensure safe ids and persisted JSON under runtime/actions. This enables an Action Editor UI to safely edit defaults without mutating them.
acceptance: Backend exposes `PUT /api/actions/<action_id>` (or `POST .../update`) accepting editable fields (name/tool/prompt/script/inputs_schema/outputs_schema).
Editing a default action creates a new user action file and returns `new_action_id` plus the created action; defaults remain unchanged on disk.
Editing a user action updates the user action file and returns the updated action.
WS broadcast emitted for updates/creation (e.g., `action_updated` or reuse `action_created` when copy-on-edit occurs).
Unit test covers: default copy-on-edit + user update-in-place + invalid id rejection.
No TCP binds required; `python3 -m py_compile` and unit tests pass.

title: PWA: Action Editor (prompt/script/tool)
notes: Add a minimal Action Editor modal to view/edit the selected block’s action template (name/tool/prompt/script). When saving edits to a default action, call the backend update endpoint and automatically switch the selected block to reference the returned `new_action_id` (copy-on-edit). Keep UI small, light-theme friendly, and fully i18n’d.
acceptance: PWA provides an Action Editor UI entrypoint (e.g., button on a STEP block) showing current action fields.
Saving calls the backend action update endpoint; if copy-on-edit returns `new_action_id`, the block’s `action_id` is updated and the pipeline script/AST is re-rendered accordingly.
Action list refreshes so the new user action appears without page reload.
All new UI strings are localized across required languages.
No TCP binds required; `node --check autonovelwriter/pwa/app.js` passes.

title: Runner: FOREACH_ACTION semantics + var scopes
notes: Implement real FOREACH_ACTION semantics: for each task, iterate over `task.actions` (list of action_ids or action refs) and execute nested children with an action-scope var namespace. Persist ActionResult with explicit inputs/outputs/artifacts, and ensure next steps consume prior outputs via vars (not folder scanning). Keep execution as stubs (no real LLM calls) but make state/resume correct.
acceptance: Runner executes FOREACH_ACTION children once per entry in `task.actions` (within FOREACH_TASK), setting `ctx.action_id`/`ctx.action_index` appropriately.
ActionResult records include action-loop metadata (e.g., `phase: 'foreach_action'`, `action_index`, `action_id_ref`).
Vars include `prev` and stable per-scope namespaces (task-scope vs action-scope) so downstream steps can explicitly consume outputs.
Resumability: restarting runner does not duplicate committed ActionResults (idempotent exec_id).
Unit test simulates a task with multiple actions and asserts cursor advancement + ActionResult persistence + var passing.
No TCP binds required; `python3 -m py_compile` and unit tests pass.

title: Project settings: extend novel overrides (inherit)
notes: Extend per-project settings beyond novel language to include a small set of novel-writing preferences (e.g., tone, target_length_words). Keep the inherit semantics consistent: empty/unset => inherit global `settings.novel.*`. Update backend validation and PWA Settings UI with explicit inherit options where needed.
acceptance: Backend `/api/projects/settings` supports additional fields (e.g., `novel_tone`, `novel_target_length_words`) with empty/unset meaning inherit global.
Backend validates numeric ranges/types for added fields and rejects invalid inputs with clear errors.
PWA Settings modal exposes the new project override fields with an inherit option/state (does not accidentally persist overrides).
Any new UI strings are localized across required languages.
Unit test covers precedence: project override wins, else global fallback.
No TCP binds required; python/js syntax checks and unit test pass.
